headline: The Order of Time takes October.
deck: Nine candidates, eleven forced-rank ballots — our biggest turnout yet. The winner takes it on breadth rather than passion, and a three-way tie for third defeats every tiebreaker in the memo.
intro: All — eleven of you ranked the candidates this round, the largest field we've had. Borda count is below. The Order of Time (Rovelli) takes October with 66 points, four clear of Inventing the Renaissance (Palmer) at 62. No tie at the top, so no tiebreaker was needed.
outcome: Winner: The Order of Time (66)   ·   Runner-up: Inventing the Renaissance (62)   ·   Relegated: none — field of nine
tieIntro: Easy Money, The Laws of Thought and The Black Count all finished on 59 points. The methodology calls for a Condorcet head-to-head — and this time it has nothing to offer, because the three of them form a perfect loop. Each beats one and loses to the other, every margin 6–5:
tieVerdict: Rock, paper, scissors. Happily nothing hinged on it — the tie is for third, all three stay on the candidate list, and the field of nine means no relegations. So we are recording a three-way third and moving on. Worth one more note in the interest of full disclosure: The Order of Time won the Borda count outright but is not a strict Condorcet winner — it beats seven of its eight rivals head-to-head and loses to The Black Count 5–6. Borda is our stated method and it named a winner cleanly, so the pairwise quirk is a curiosity, not a dispute.
notes: The winner is not a strict Condorcet winner. The Order of Time wins the Borda count outright, and beats seven of its eight rivals head-to-head — but loses to The Black Count 5–6. Borda is the club's stated method and it produced a clean winner with a four-point margin, so this is a curiosity rather than a dispute. It is recorded here because the pairwise table is part of the round.

Consensus over passion. The Order of Time took just one first-place vote and no last-place finishes; it won on the strength of eleven middling-to-high placements. Say Nothing led the field on first-place votes with three and still finished sixth. The Order of Time placed seventh in the September poll on 38 points.

Mean rank cannot break a Borda tie. The three tied books show identical mean ranks of 4.64 — necessarily, since Borda points are a linear function of rank (points = 10 − rank, so equal totals force equal means). Mean rank is a restatement of the Borda score, not an independent breaker, and it will tie every time the score does.
